列朝詩集/丙09.poet_heading: ==[[Author:唐寅|唐解元寅]] 七十五首==
列朝詩集/丙09.verdict: NOT a disjoint training split. 24 of 25 are the SAME Wikisource pages the held-out corpus was built from — the anthology transcludes them rather than carrying its own text.

wikisource_alternative.列朝詩集/丙08: NO 唐寅 poet section. The 唐寅 hit there is a POEM TITLE linking to him (用韻答[[Author:唐寅|伯虎]]) — another poet writing TO him. My first pass read that as a poet heading and counted 25 poems that are not his; corrected here.

conclusion: A training split for 唐寅 that is disjoint from the held-out set cannot be had from Wikisource, and ctext — which has four relevant editions — is closed to us without a subscription. The study's train/held-out separation is blocked on a spend decision or a re-cut of the design.
options_for_ri_and_louay: (a) SUBSCRIBE to ctext (institutional; their page says libraries normally fund it). Gives an authenticated JSON API and, in their words, more accurate data than scraping. Louay's call — spend.

(b) RE-CUT: drop the 'held-out SOURCE' framing and take a random split of the one corpus we can get (103 blocks). Cheap, honest, but the contamination story changes: the split is no longer a different edition.

(c) The 集外詩 tail of 列朝詩集/丙09 (the LINKED, non-transcluded titles, 28 of them) is the only Wikisource material that may be disjoint. It is small and I have NOT verified its disjointness — that is a measurement, not a claim.
bounds: Wikisource returned HTTP 429 once during this work. Everything since is backed off (8-15 s between requests). Nothing was hammered.
The 24-of-25 overlap is measured on PAGE TITLE identity, not on text. Two pages with different titles could still carry the same poem.
I corrected my own first reading of 列朝詩集/丙08 before publishing it; the wrong version never left this box.
